description: A tool's `expect:` CEL expression reads a JSON-parsed integer too large for CEL's 64-bit `int` (`_to_cel`'s own `ValueError("overflow")`, raised uncaught by `evaluate_cel_expect` -- not a `CelEvaluationError`). `core/tool.py`'s attempt loop catches it exactly like any other attempt exception: the attempt fails and retries up to `retries.max_attempts`, `meta.error` reads "overflow" (not "expect failed: ..."), and `meta.expect` is never set on the failed attempt (a failed, non-raising expectation sets it; this never reaches that code). The exhausted last attempt's bare `ValueError` propagates through `on_error: fail` with no extra wrapping of its own.
